Health guidance
The main things to keep in mind right now, based on how you have been feeling.
Personalized for Margaret
Margaret, you're recovering from knee surgery while managing hypertension and diabetes. Right now, your body needs extra protein to heal the surgical site, and stable blood sugar to support your energy. We've tailored everything below specifically for your situation — please trust the process, even when your appetite is low.
🥩
Prioritize protein at every meal — even a few bites count
→ Your knee is still healing. Protein repairs tissue and prevents muscle loss while you're less active.
🧂
Keep meals low in salt — aim for less than 5g per day
→ With your blood pressure at 138/85, reducing salt helps your medication work better and protects your heart.
🫒
Choose steamed, boiled, or baked over fried
→ Your cholesterol levels benefit from less oil. Steaming also keeps food soft and easy to eat when appetite is low.
💧
Drink warm water or herbal tea throughout the day
→ Hydration helps your kidneys process medication (metformin) and reduces the nausea you've been experiencing.
🚶
Even a 5-minute walk counts as progress
→ After knee surgery, any gentle movement prevents stiffness and helps blood glucose come down naturally.
Suggestions
Simple next steps that may feel the most helpful today.
Appetite decreased Low activity level Glucose monitoring gaps

Take metformin right in the middle of a meal (not before or after) to reduce nausea
▶
💬 You've reported nausea twice after taking metformin on an empty stomach. Mid-meal timing significantly reduces GI side effects during post-surgery recovery.
🥗
Try eating 5-6 small meals instead of 3 big ones — even a few bites count
▶
💬 Your appetite has decreased since surgery. Smaller, frequent meals are easier to tolerate and help maintain blood glucose stability with your diabetes.
🏃
Do 10 minutes of seated leg exercises twice a day to keep your muscles active
▶
💬 After your knee replacement 6 weeks ago, gentle movement prevents muscle atrophy and improves circulation, which supports healing and glucose regulation.
🏃
Take a short 5-minute walk around your home when you feel up to it
▶
💬 Light walking — even indoors — promotes knee recovery, reduces blood pressure, and helps counter the low activity pattern we've noticed over the past 5 days.
📋
Set a daily alarm for glucose checking — consistency helps your doctor adjust your plan
▶
💬 You missed glucose checks on 3 days this period. Regular data helps your doctor decide if your metformin dosage needs adjustment.
🏠
Ask your daughter to help prep some easy grab-and-go snacks for the week
▶
💬 Since you live alone and haven't been going out, having pre-made nutritious snacks removes the barrier of cooking when you're fatigued.
